source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade and downgrade via broadcom tools in Linux OS
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Put fw tool in Linux OS
$unzip g4Xdiagnostics_linux.zip
2. Check PCIe Switch Firmware file into the same folder. (Please check the veriosn should be the latest one.)
Miramar_PCIe_SW1_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw Miramar_PCIe_SW2_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
Miramar_PCIe_SW3_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
Miramar_PCIe_SW4_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw
3. There are four PCIe Switches (PEX89144) in the system, please list and check PCIe Switches as below command.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 --list
It should show eight PEX89144 devices as below picture.
The devices 1 and 2 belong to PCIe Switch 1 (SW1).
The devices 3 and 4 belong to PCIe Switch 2 (SW2).
The devices 5 and 6 belong to PCIe Switch 3 (SW3).
The devices 7 and 8 belong to PCIe Switch 4 (SW4).
4. Updated PCIe SW1-4 firmware image.
Before updating, you may need to check current PCIe SW1 firmware version as below command.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 1 show
Updating the required firmware to SW1 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 1 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW1_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW2 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 3 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW2_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW3 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 5 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW3_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
Updating the required firmware to SW4 as below command and check result.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i 7 dl -f Miramar_PCIe_SW4_signed_vB.07_20240126_135128.fw -s
5. Restart the system to make the fresh image active.
# reboot
6. The PCIe Switch 1-4 (SW1-4) firmware version should be updated as expected.
# ./g4Xdiagnostics.x86_64 -i [1,3,5,7] show

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. The firmware should be updated without any error and worked as expected.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO based on an unrelated physical plug-cycle, not this Broadcom firmware procedure.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; restores actual g4Xdiagnostics scope and adds image, mapping, rollback and OOB gates.
historical_reviews.round_02: NO inherited from mismatched DeepSeek content.

original_test_intent: Use Broadcom g4Xdiagnostics in Linux to program the four PEX89144 switch firmware images, activate by reboot, and prove the expected versions and PCIe health; the title additionally claims both upgrade and downgrade coverage.
original_method: Validate the exact vendor tool, signed per-switch images, device-pair mapping and rollback/OOB recovery; serialize approved writes to indices 1/3/5/7 with full logs, reboot once, then re-enumerate versions/topology and events.
manual_activity: One authorized user approves the exact images, direction and recovery plan. Tool staging, enumeration, writes, reboot and verification are machine-executable; destructive approval does not make the core PARTIAL.
required_inputs: Compatible vendor g4Xdiagnostics build and usage documentation
Signed/checksummed SW1-SW4 images and approved upgrade/downgrade matrix
Verified PEX89144 pair-to-switch mapping for this chassis
Current versions/topology, dedicated workload window and stable power
Rollback images, OOB/vendor recovery and final approval
safety_requirements: Do not infer that B.07 is latest or compatible; validate signatures, checksums, board IDs and direction per switch.
Stop before writes if enumeration is not exactly understood or any mapping/image/recovery fact is incomplete.
Serialize writes and retain per-target output; stop on the first error and do not flash remaining switches automatically.
Do not retry, power-cycle, substitute images or issue recovery writes without a new approved plan.
Reboot only after approved successful writes and keep OOB access throughout activation.
agent_execution_scope: Validate tool, package hashes, image signatures/matrix, mapping, baselines and recovery readiness.
Execute each approved `show`/`dl` transaction and activation reboot with complete raw evidence and Safety Stop.
Re-enumerate versions/topology/events and report Tool Result without formal PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve tool/image provenance, mapping, upgrade versus downgrade targets and recovery plan.
Authorize disposition after any failed write or activation issue.
Review post-flash evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No fit: it reviews unrelated physical board handling and would discard the actual firmware workflow.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve `--list`, per-index `show`, four explicit `dl -f ... -s` commands and reboot; validate `[1,3,5,7]` multi-index show syntax before using it.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Tool archive, four filenames, eight-device mapping, indices 1/3/5/7, commands, reboot, criterion and 5/15-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: ORIGINAL VENDOR FLASH PATH RETAINED WITH SUPPLY-CHAIN AND RECOVERY GATES
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a signed manifest binding each chassis switch identity and current/target/rollback version, then perform one audited write at a time followed by a single controlled activation and topology verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The documented PEX89144/Miramar platform only after vendor compatibility confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record g4Xdiagnostics build/hash, image hashes/signatures, switch silicon/board revision, BIOS/BMC/OS/kernel and PCIe topology.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Broadcom/vendor platform documentation supplied with the approved package; public equivalence is not assumed.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds supply-chain validation, explicit direction matrix, immutable mapping, serial fail-stop behavior and rollback readiness.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; downgrade must be separately demonstrated if required by the title.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Vendor package, signed images and supported upgrade/downgrade matrix.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect mapping or image can remove multiple downstream PCIe paths and require vendor recovery.

project_override_considerations: Projects may select a subset or different approved versions, but must report each direction/target. An upgrade-only run cannot claim downgrade coverage.
expected_evidence: Tool/image hashes/signatures, support matrix, chassis mapping, eight-device list and pre-versions/topology
Per-switch approved direction, exact show/dl stdout/stderr/return code and timestamps
Activation reboot state and post-version for indices 1/3/5/7
Post PCIe topology/device availability and OS/BMC event comparison
Rollback readiness, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title requires `Upgrade and downgrade`, while the procedure only shows programming one set described as latest and has no reverse/downgrade sequence or acceptance. The master wording is preserved and the missing direction must be resolved by the owner.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The firmware-write intent is clear and reviewable; direction and artifacts are execution-readiness inputs. Do not execute until the approved matrix resolves actual coverage.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects the unrelated physical-case analysis and restores the true Broadcom firmware scope.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains all flash/recovery safeguards while correcting approval-gated PARTIAL to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automation capability, readiness, Tool Result and engineer verdict and explicitly records upgrade/downgrade source conflict.

review_improvement: Prevents a multi-switch firmware test from being lost to an unrelated manual classification and prevents an upgrade-only procedure from silently satisfying downgrade coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Every core step is software-controlled once vendor artifacts and recovery are approved. Firmware risk affects approval and Safety Stop, not capability; the incomplete downgrade method is a real source conflict, not grounds to invent commands.

source_provenance.history: review_round_02_functionality.md exact-code entry and repository exact-code search

no_automatic_retry: Do not retry a flash, continue to another switch after error, guess an index/image, power-cycle blindly or apply rollback without a newly approved recovery plan.
